```{r, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
# 'config' is the file sourced by wf_rrbs.py (gse, project, species, annotation, version, ...)
source("config")
# Safeguards: variables that may be missing from 'config'
if (!exists("sequencer")) sequencer = "<SEQUENCER>"
if (!exists("seqlen")) seqlen = "<READ_LENGTH>"
if (!exists("conda_env")) conda_env = "rrbs_env"
```

```{r software_versions, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
# Retrieve the versions of the software tools actually installed.
# Strategy: 1) 'conda list' of the environment 'conda_env' (reflects what the workflow ran with),
#           2) fallback on the '--version' output of the command found in the PATH.
# NB: knit this vignette from a shell where the conda environment is activated
#     (or make sure 'conda' is available) to get all the versions.

conda_list = tryCatch({
  out = suppressWarnings(system2("conda", c("list", "-n", conda_env), stdout=TRUE, stderr=FALSE))
  out = trimws(out[!grepl("^#", out) & nzchar(out)])
  fields = strsplit(out, "\\s+")
  setNames(sapply(fields, `[`, 2), sapply(fields, `[`, 1))
}, error=function(e) character(0))

cmd_version = function(cmd, args="--version") {
  if (!nzchar(Sys.which(cmd))) return(NA_character_)
  out = tryCatch(suppressWarnings(system2(cmd, args, stdout=TRUE, stderr=TRUE)), error=function(e) character(0))
  out = paste(out, collapse="\n")
  m = regmatches(out, regexec("(?i)version:?\\s*v?([0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)+)", out, perl=TRUE))[[1]]
  if (length(m) >= 2) return(m[2])
  m = regmatches(out, regexpr("[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)+", out))
  if (length(m)) return(m[1])
  NA_character_
}

get_version = function(pkg, cmd=pkg, args="--version") {
  ver = if (pkg %in% names(conda_list)) unname(conda_list[pkg]) else NA_character_
  if (is.na(ver)) ver = cmd_version(cmd, args)
  ver
}

# tool label, conda package, command used as a fallback
tools = data.frame(
  key     = c("fastqc", "multiqc", "trimgalore", "cutadapt", "bismark", "bowtie2", "samtools", "bg2bw", "deeptools", "snakemake", "slurm"),
  tool    = c("FastQC", "MultiQC", "Trim Galore", "Cutadapt", "Bismark", "Bowtie2", "samtools", "bedGraphToBigWig", "deepTools", "Snakemake", "SLURM"),
  pkg     = c("fastqc", "multiqc", "trim-galore", "cutadapt", "bismark", "bowtie2", "samtools", "ucsc-bedgraphtobigwig", "deeptools", "snakemake", NA),
  cmd     = c("fastqc", "multiqc", "trim_galore", "cutadapt", "bismark", "bowtie2", "samtools", "bedGraphToBigWig", "bamCoverage", "snakemake", "sbatch"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
tools$version = sapply(seq_len(nrow(tools)), function(i) {
  ver = if (!is.na(tools$pkg[i])) get_version(tools$pkg[i], tools$cmd[i]) else cmd_version(tools$cmd[i])
  ver
})
tools$version[tools$key == "slurm"] = sub("^slurm\\s*", "", tools$version[tools$key == "slurm"])

# R and conda
r_version = paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep=".")
conda_version = cmd_version("conda")

# Named list used inline in the text: `r v$bismark`
v = as.list(setNames(tools$version, tools$key))
v = lapply(v, function(x) if (is.na(x)) "<VERSION>" else x)
v$conda = ifelse(is.na(conda_version), "<VERSION>", conda_version)
v$R = r_version
```

# Material and Methods

**Quality control of raw reads**

The quality of the raw fastq files (R1 and R2) was assessed using `FastQC` v`r v$fastqc` [https://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/fastqc/. Accessed 19 Oct. 2026.]. Reports of all samples were aggregated using `MultiQC` v`r v$multiqc` (Ewels et al. 2016) [PMID: 27312411].

**Trimming**

The raw paired-end fastq files were quality- and adapter-trimmed using `Trim Galore` v`r v$trimgalore` [https://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/trim_galore/. Accessed 19 Oct. 2026.] (a wrapper around `Cutadapt` v`r v$cutadapt` (Martin 2011) [doi: 10.14806/ej.17.1.200]), with options `--paired --fastqc --cores 4`. Only read pairs for which both mates passed the filters were kept (validated pairs, `*_R1_val_1.fq.gz` and `*_R2_val_2.fq.gz`). A second `FastQC` report was generated on the trimmed reads.

**Bisulfite genome preparation**

The `r annotation` `r species` `r version` reference genome was converted *in silico* into its bisulfite counterparts (C-to-T and G-to-A conversions) and indexed using `bismark_genome_preparation` (`Bismark` suite v`r v$bismark`; Krueger and Andrews 2011) [PMID: 21493656], with option `--bowtie2`.

**Alignment**

The trimmed paired-end reads were aligned on the `r annotation` `r species` `r version` bisulfite genome using `Bismark` v`r v$bismark` (Krueger and Andrews 2011) [PMID: 21493656] with the `Bowtie2` v`r v$bowtie2` aligner (Langmead and Salzberg 2012) [PMID: 22388286], with options `--non_directional --multicore 16`. The `--non_directional` mode allows reads to align to any of the four possible bisulfite strands.

Resulting BAM files were coordinate-sorted and indexed using `samtools sort` and `samtools index` (`samtools` v`r v$samtools`; Li et al. 2009) [PMID: 19505943].

**Deduplication**

BAM files were sorted by read name using `samtools sort -n`, and duplicated read pairs (same alignment start position) were removed using `deduplicate_bismark` (`Bismark` suite v`r v$bismark`) with option `-p` (paired-end mode).

**Methylation calling**

Cytosine methylation calls were extracted from the deduplicated BAM files using `bismark_methylation_extractor` (`Bismark` suite v`r v$bismark`; Krueger and Andrews 2011) [PMID: 21493656], with options `--bedGraph --counts --gzip --comprehensive --parallel 32`. Methylation calls of all contexts (CpG, CHG, CHH) were pooled into one file per strand-specific context (`--comprehensive`). This step produced, for each sample:

- a splitting report (`*.deduplicated_splitting_report.txt`),

- an M-bias report (`*.deduplicated.M-bias.txt`),

- a deduplication report (`*.deduplication_report.txt`),

- a bedGraph file of the CpG methylation levels (`*.deduplicated.bedGraph.gz`),

- a coverage file (`*.deduplicated.bismark.cov.gz`).

**CpG strand merging**

CpG methylation counts of the two strands of each CpG dinucleotide were merged into a single CpG-level evidence using `coverage2cytosine` (from the `Bismark` suite v`r v$bismark`) with options `--merge_CpGs --gzip` and the `r annotation` `r species` `r version` genome sequence (`merged_CpG_evidence.cov.gz` files).

**Processed data files format and content**

- BAM files (`.bam`, `.bai`): deduplicated and sorted aligned reads,

- bedGraph files (`.bedGraph.gz`): CpG methylation level (percentage) per position,

- big wig files (`.bw`): bedGraph files converted using `bedGraphToBigWig` v`r v$bg2bw` (Kent et al. 2010) [PMID: 20639541] and the chromosome size file of the `r version` genome (`r version`.chrom.sizes),

- coverage files (`.merged_CpG_evidence.cov.gz`): strand-merged methylated and unmethylated CpG counts per position (chromosome, start, end, methylation percentage, count methylated, count unmethylated).

**Read coverage tracks**

Read coverage signal was computed from the sorted BAM files using `bamCoverage` (from the `deepTools` suite v`r v$deeptools` (Ramirez et al. 2014) [PMID: 24799436]), with options `--binSize 4 --minMappingQuality 30 --normalizeUsing RPKM`.

**Workflow management and computing environment**

The whole analysis was orchestrated using `Snakemake` v`r v$snakemake` (Mölder et al. 2021) [PMID: 34035898]. Software tools were run in a dedicated `conda` v`r v$conda` environment (`r conda_env`). Computing jobs were scheduled using `SLURM` v`r v$slurm`, with intermediate files processed on node-local scratch storage. Statistical analyses and report generation were performed using `R` v`r v$R`.

The workflow code is available at [https://github.com/fchuffar/pipeline_dnam](https://github.com/fchuffar/pipeline_dnam).

# Software versions

```{r software_table, results="asis"}
tab = rbind(
  data.frame(Software=tools$tool, Version=ifelse(is.na(tools$version), "not found", tools$version)),
  data.frame(Software=c("conda", "R"), Version=c(ifelse(is.na(conda_version), "not found", conda_version), r_version))
)
tab = tab[order(tab$Software), ]
rownames(tab) = NULL
knitr::kable(tab)
```

Versions were retrieved automatically from the `r conda_env` conda environment (`conda list`) or, when unavailable, from the `--version` output of the tools found in the `PATH`. The `bismark_genome_preparation`, `deduplicate_bismark`, `bismark_methylation_extractor` and `coverage2cytosine` tools belong to the `Bismark` suite and share its version.
